To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DNA microarrays were successfully used to estimate mRNA concentrations for all known competence genes of Streptococcuspneumoe in response to competence-stimulating factor (CSP).
DNA microarrays can be used to monitor the expression of many genes at once and that the genes that are induced during competence are not all regulated by a common mechanism.
the expression of the comAB, comCD, and comX genes is induced in a sequential manner and that the comAB operon may be involved in the regulation of the expression of the other two operons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of genes required for the competence regulon of S. pneumoniae and with the timing of the induction of these genes.

the regulation of the competence cycle and provides the first comprehensive view of the expression of all genes associated with competence during the induction of competence by the competence-stimulation peptide
the regulation of competence for DNA uptake in Streptococcuspneumoniae
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

competence in S. pneumoniae is regulated at the level of gene expression by a complex network of regulatory genes, which in turn control expression of a large group of genes required for transformation.

the competence genes in S. pneumoniae are induced sequentially in a cascade of events that begins with the expression of the comAB, comCD, and comX genes and ends with the induction of the DNA-processing-pathway genes.
competence in S. pneumoniae is controlled by at least three different regulatory mechanisms, each of which may be activated by CSP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

(i) the competence regulon is composed of at least 40 genes, (ii) the expression of these genes is controlled by a cascade of at least three transcriptional regulators, and (iii) the expression of all competence genes is induced within the first 12 min of exposure to CSP
the competence regulons of S. pneumoniae are induced sequentially and that the expression of the target genes depends on the ComX sigma factor.
CSP induces a rapid expression of a set of competence regulatory genes that, in turn, induce the competence target genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the competence genes in S. pneumoniae are expressed in a coordinated fashion.
DNA microarrays can be used to study gene expression in a variety of organisms, including bacteria, in a relatively straightforward manner.
DNA microarrays provide a useful tool for the study of the complex regulatory networks that control the expression of genes in response to environmental signals.
